 1960s Books
 8mm Bolex Cine Guide
 Paperback: 62 pages
 Publisher: Paillard S.A. (1962)
 Language: English
 This book was originally included free with the purchase of an 8mm Bolex camera. Not nearly as in-depth as the original Cine Guide, this version covers only the basics of making home movies. However, it contains many photographs and brightly colored illustrations. 
 An Introduction to Home Movies
 Raymond C. Lawson
 Paperback: 32 pages
 Publisher: Paillard Incorporated, NY (1962)
 Language: English
 This booklet contains a series of articles that originally appeared in the Bolex Reporter. The articles were published in ten installments over a three year period, and were featured in Vol 9, No 1 through Vol 11, No 2. According to the cover, the editors of the Bolex Reporter received many requests from readers to combine the series into a compact reference book that could be carried in a camera case. Copies were sent free of charge by writing to Paillard Inc., NY. 
 Bolex 8 Guide
 G. R. Sharp
 Hardcover: 112 pages
 Publisher: Focal Press Ltd. (4th edition, 1962)
 Language: English
 This edition of the Focal Press Bolex 8 Guide features a hard plastic cover. Although not shown here, a paper dust jacket was included that covers the lower half of the book. Like earlier editions, this book focuses on the operation and use of Bolex pocket size cameras and is updated with the latest models.
 Cover scan: Courtesy of Helmuth Porschen.
 Bolex 8 Guide
 G. R. Sharp
 Paperback: 120 pages
 Publisher: Focal Press Ltd. (5th edition, 1966)
 Language: English
 The fifth and final edition of the Bolex 8 Guide included the full range of pocket size Bolex cameras, as well as the Zoom Reflex and Automatic 8mm cameras such as the K2. It originally sold for 12s. 6d. in 1966 in Britain.
 Cover scan: Courtesy of Helmuth Porschen.
 Bolex H16-H8 Guide
 A. J. Surgenor
 Paperback: 127 pages
 Publisher: Focal Press Ltd. (8th edition, 1967)
 Language: English
 Revised by Paul Petzold, the eighth edition of the Focal Press Guide was expanded to include information on the latest changes to H-8 and H-16 cameras. Like previous editions, it is fully illustrated and offers operating advice on the cameras and their accessories, as well as general tips and techniques for filming.
